data.narrative: Student Alekhya Tentu demonstrated mastery in high-throughput caching and performance optimization throughout Module 06. Selected Option A (Cache-Aside) for memory efficiency and lazy population, implemented post-commit cache invalidation on link mutations, accurately diagnosed the injected cache staleness bug, engineered resilient DB fallback during cache outages, and verified all 45 automated regression tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected Option A (Cache-Aside) based on the 80/20 link access distribution, weighing lazy memory loading against first-read cache miss penalties.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student stated: 'I choose Cache-Aside because our URL shortener may contain millions of links, but only a small percentage are accessed frequently (80/20 rule). This caches only frequently requested links instead of loading every link into Redis, reducing memory usage.'

dimension_scores.observation: Immediately identified the root cause of stale redirects following link update: pinpointed missing cache invalidation call in update_link without requiring hints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student accurately diagnosed: 'The breakdown occurred during cache invalidation after the database update. The old Redis entry was not deleted or refreshed.'

dimension_scores.observation: Addressed the constraints twist by ensuring tenant isolation in cache keys, preventing cross-tenant cache pollution, and warning against caching auth-protected data without authorization checks.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student explained: 'If cache keys do not include tenant identity, one organization may access another organization's cached data... tenant-scoped keys and permission-based invalidation are essential.'

dimension_scores.observation: Advocated for post-commit cache invalidation to defeat race conditions, recognized TTL as a crucial safety backstop, and identified Cache Stampede risks with single-flight locking mitigations.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student stated: 'Cache invalidation must happen after the PostgreSQL transaction successfully commits. Invalidating before commit creates a race condition where another request reads the old DB value and repopulates Redis with stale data.'

dimension_scores.observation: Communicated distributed systems concepts, race conditions, cache lifecycles, and mitigation strategies with professional engineering clarity.
dimension_scores.evidence: Articulated thundering herd risks and concrete mitigations: request coalescing, TTL jitter, and connection pooling.

strengths: Flawless cache diagnosis: accurately isolated the omitted invalidation hook on link update without hints.
Mature concurrency instincts: correctly identified the pre-commit vs. post-commit invalidation race condition.
Comprehensive verification: verified Cache-Aside MISS -> HIT -> Invalidation -> Fallback across 45 automated tests.
growth_areas: Ready to tackle Module 07: Background Jobs & Async Processing to offload click analytics from the critical redirect path using message queues.
data.recommendation: Advance to Module 07: Background Jobs & Async Processing to decouple analytics persistence using asynchronous workers.

public_evidence.student_action: Engineered Cache-Aside resolution with 300s TTL, post-commit mutation invalidation hooks, and graceful DB fallback with 45 passing automated tests.
public_evidence.proof: Passed 45/45 pytest suite; live verification confirmed X-Cache: MISS on first read, X-Cache: HIT on second read, immediate eviction on PATCH, and seamless DB fallback during Redis outages.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves ability to design sub-millisecond hot-path caching with Redis, eliminate cache staleness bugs, handle distributed race conditions, and build resilient fallbacks.
